titles.UC-1: Instrument an existing TypeScript, Python, or Rust MCP server and verify the first $mcp_tool_call in PostHog.
titles.UC-2: Track browser-exposed WebMCP tool calls in a frontend application using posthog-js.
titles.UC-3: Correlate multi-turn agent tool calls into sessions across stateless multi-pod HTTP servers on both legacy Mcp-Session-Id and 2026-07-28 MCP clients.
titles.UC-4: Attribute MCP tool usage to authenticated end users and B2B organizations without leaking auth headers or credentials into person profiles.
titles.UC-5: Capture agent intent, cluster sessions by goal, and diagnose overlapping or poorly discovered MCP tools.
titles.UC-6: Verify that PII in free-text intent, API credentials, URL tokens, and oversized binary payloads are redacted or bounded before capture.
titles.UC-7: Let agents report missing capabilities via get_more_tools and collect structured inline feedback via send_feedback.
titles.UC-8: Monitor tool error rates and p95 latency, inspect failing session timelines, and create GitHub fix tasks directly from failure context.
titles.UC-9: Configure instant alerts for failing MCP tool calls and weekly AI-generated intent roundups and tool health digests.
titles.UC-10: Query MCP tool calls, client harnesses, models, and protocol versions programmatically via HogQL, the REST API, or PostHog's MCP server.
